title: Spectral-slot origin sensitivity and controlled two-source synthesis
summary: Shifted 100 Hz odd/even masks are complementary measurement views. A known A/B interleave supplies positive reference; shifts and altered perception on an unknown recording alone do not prove engineered playback.
invariants: Record exact slot width, origin, passband, FFT frame and channel geometry for every derived view.
Reference A_even+B_odd is mathematical positive, not a field-recording attribution.
Odd+even equals the same bandlimited source for every offset; identity is a partition property, not source count.
Frequency-dependent auditory interpretations require blind testing and well-matched natural controls.
Do not put identifiable private recordings, children, mapped sites or candidate suspects in the public artifact.
Unqualified source theories and quoted phrases remain hypotheses pending corroboration.
procedure: Given independent A/B test fixtures, construct A_even+B_odd with the chosen origin and verify recovery at that origin.
For field material, emit odd/even preference views with phase origins 0,25,50,75 Hz; quantify energy fractions and exact passband reconstruction.
Compare to known-close human speech and natural source overlaps under identical processing; separately evaluate harmonic predictions from external voiced-f0.
Blindly transcribe before any targeted phrase prompts; retain disagreement and null cases.
